_comment: Shared base for trigger templates. Trigger JSONs can set "extends": "trigger_base" and will be deep-merged with this object (template wins).

create_trigger.description: Create a new trigger using this template

app_id.description: UUID of your Piwik PRO app

attributes.description: Trigger configuration object. Must include name, trigger_type, and conditions as required by this template (see required_attributes). Use tools_parameters_get("triggers_create") for the full runtime JSON schema. For each conditions[].variable_id: built-in variables → conditions_reference.conditions.<key>.builtin_variable_id; custom variables → variables_list(app_id, filters={"builtin": false}).

relationships.description: Optional MCP tool argument (top-level only; never nest under attributes). May include only ``triggers`` and/or ``tags``; other keys are rejected. Values are validated and expanded into JSON:API ``data`` arrays.

triggers.description: Optional. Related triggers (JSON:API triggers relationship). Each item is either a UUID string or an object with id (UUID) and optional meta.

meta.description: Optional per-link metadata on the relationship member

firing_threshold.description: Firing threshold for this linked trigger (>= 1)

tags.description: Optional. Tag resource UUIDs to attach to this trigger (JSON:API tags relationship).

notes: Omit relationships entirely if you do not need tag or trigger links at creation time.
Only the keys triggers and tags are allowed; use tools_parameters_get if your client needs the exact schema.
Use assets in favor of fetching resources when in need for references. Fetch only if you are stuck.

update_trigger.description: Update an existing trigger - only editable fields can be modified

app_id.description: The Piwik PRO app ID containing the trigger

trigger_id.description: The UUID of the trigger to update

attributes.description: Trigger fields to update (only editable fields are processed): optional name and conditions. Use tools_parameters_get("triggers_update") for the runtime JSON schema. Do not put relationships here; use the top-level relationships parameter. When updating conditions[], resolve variable_id the same way as triggers_create (built-in → conditions_reference.conditions.<key>.builtin_variable_id; custom → variables_list with builtin=false).

relationships.description: Optional MCP tool argument (top-level only). Same as triggers_create: only optional ``triggers`` and/or ``tags``; other keys are rejected.

triggers.description: Optional. Same items as triggers_create: UUID strings and/or {id, meta?} objects with meta.firing_threshold >= 1 when meta is set. Use an empty array to clear the triggers relationship on a relationship-only update.

tags.description: Optional. Tag UUIDs. Use an empty array to clear the tags relationship when you are applying a relationship-only update.

update_requirements.description: At least one of optional_parameters.attributes or optional_parameters.relationships must be provided with meaningful content (e.g. a non-empty attributes object, or relationships with at least one list key set, including an empty list to clear links).

notes: Use assets in favor of fetching resources when in need for references. Fetch only if you are stuck.

name.description: Human-readable trigger name that describes its purpose
name.recommendation: Use descriptive names that clearly indicate what is being tracked

trigger_type.edit_note: ⚠️ Cannot be changed after trigger creation

conditions.description: Array of condition objects that define when the trigger should fire. Look for definitions in: conditions_reference

condition_id.description: Unique identifier for this condition (auto-generated during trigger creation)

variable_id.description: UUID of the variable to check. Built-in: copy builtin_variable_id from the matching conditions_reference.conditions entry. Custom: use id from variables_list(app_id, filters={"builtin": false}).

value.description: Operand for the comparison. Unary condition types (which are only: is_true, is_false, is_set, is_not_set, is_empty, is_not_empty), require JSON null.

anyOf.description: Only for condition types: is_true, is_false, is_set, is_not_set, is_empty, is_not_empty.

created_at.description: When the trigger was created (ISO 8601 timestamp)
created_at.edit_note: 🚫 Auto-generated by API, cannot be modified

updated_at.description: When the trigger was last updated (ISO 8601 timestamp)
updated_at.edit_note: 🚫 Auto-generated by API, cannot be modified

is_published.description: Whether the trigger is published in the current version
is_published.edit_note: 🚫 Controlled by version publishing, cannot be directly modified

field_mutability_guide.description: Understanding which trigger fields can be edited after creation

editable.description: ✅ Can be updated anytime after trigger creation
editable.note: These fields can be safely modified through triggers_update (attributes) or relationship lists via the top-level relationships parameter

create-only.description: ⚠️ Can only be set during trigger creation, immutable afterward
create-only.edit_behavior: These fields will be ignored in update operations
create-only.note: Trigger type defines the fundamental behavior and cannot be changed

read-only.edit_behavior: These fields will be filtered out of update requests
read-only.note: Timestamps and publishing status are managed by the system

update_best_practices: Only include editable fields in triggers_update attributes; use the top-level relationships parameter for triggers/tags UUID lists
Create-only and read-only fields are automatically filtered out
Check field mutability before attempting updates
Use templates_get_trigger() to see all available fields and their mutability
Test trigger conditions after updates to ensure they work as expected

variable_reference_guide.description: How to resolve conditions[].variable_id when creating or updating triggers.

builtin_variables.how_to_load: templates_get_trigger(template_name='...') — trigger_base is merged into trigger templates and includes conditions_reference.
steps: Read conditions_reference (below) or the trigger template's available_event_conditions / required_conditions to find the condition key and builtin_variable_name (e.g. event → Event, page_url → Page URL).
Built-in UUIDs are fixed platform-wide; do not use variables_list for them. Do not call triggers_create until every variable_id is verified.

custom_variables.where: Tag Manager API — app-scoped user-created variables only
steps: Call variables_list with builtin=false to list custom variables for the app.
Copy the resource id from the matching variable into conditions[].variable_id.
Use when the trigger allows custom_variable_based in conditions_reference or when the condition targets a user-defined variable (data layer, constant, etc.).

variable_reference_guide.conditions_reference_link: conditions_reference.conditions[].builtin_variable_name names the built-in variable; for built-ins, copy variable_id from the adjacent builtin_variable_id field, not a guessed UUID.

condition_types_reference.description: Maps API `condition_type` values (object keys, snake_case) to metadata. Use the key string as `conditions[].condition_type`. Each entry includes `value` (same as the key), `display_name` (UI-oriented label), and documentation fields.

contains.description: Met when the condition value is a substring of the variable value.
contains.variable_value_note: The variable value must be a string, number, or boolean; otherwise this condition is never met.

does_not_contain.description: Met when the condition value is not a substring of the variable value.
does_not_contain.variable_value_note: The variable value must be a string, number, or boolean; otherwise this condition is never met.

starts_with.description: Met when the variable value starts with the condition value.
starts_with.variable_value_note: The variable value must be a string, number, or boolean; otherwise this condition is never met.

ends_with.description: Met when the variable value ends with the condition value.
ends_with.variable_value_note: The variable value must be a string, number, or boolean; otherwise this condition is never met.

equals.description: Met when the variable value equals the condition value.
equals.variable_value_note: The variable value must be a string, number, or boolean; otherwise this condition is never met.
notes: For a Traffic source variable, allowed condition values include: Direct, Referral, Social, Organic search, Campaign.

does_not_equal.description: Met when the variable value does not equal the condition value.
does_not_equal.variable_value_note: The variable value must be a string, number, or boolean; otherwise this condition is never met.
notes: For a Traffic source variable, allowed condition values include: Direct, Referral, Social, Organic search, Campaign.

regexp.description: Met when the variable value matches the given regular expression.
regexp.variable_value_note: The variable value must be a string, number, or boolean; otherwise this condition is never met.

does_not_start_with.description: Met when the variable value does not start with the condition value.
does_not_start_with.variable_value_note: The variable value must be a string, number, or boolean; otherwise this condition is never met.

does_not_end_with.description: Met when the variable value does not end with the condition value.
does_not_end_with.variable_value_note: The variable value must be a string, number, or boolean; otherwise this condition is never met.

does_not_regexp.description: Met when the variable value does not match the given regular expression.
does_not_regexp.variable_value_note: The variable value must be a string, number, or boolean; otherwise this condition is never met.

is_true.description: Met when the variable value is boolean true.
is_true.variable_value_note: If the variable value is the strings "TRUE" or "true", this condition is not met.

is_false.description: Met when the variable value is boolean false.
is_false.variable_value_note: If the variable value is the strings "FALSE" or "false", this condition is not met.

is_set.description: Met when the variable value is defined: neither null nor undefined.

is_not_set.description: Met when the variable value is undefined or null.

is_empty.description: Met when the variable value is one of: null, undefined, empty string (""), empty array ([]), empty object ({}).

is_not_empty.description: Met when the variable value is none of: null, undefined, empty string (""), empty array ([]), empty object ({}).

matches.description: Met when the clicked element matches the given selector (CSS or XPath).
notes: Available only for the Click Element variable.

does_not_match.description: Met when the clicked element does not match the given selector (CSS or XPath).
notes: Available only for the Click Element variable.

is_a_child_of.description: Met when the clicked element is a child of an element matched by the given selector (CSS or XPath). A parent element is checked recursively up to 100 elements in the DOM.
is_a_child_of.example: Click Element is a child of .footer
notes: Available only for the Click Element variable.

is_not_a_child_of.description: Met when the clicked element is not a child of an element matched by the given selector (CSS or XPath). A parent element is checked recursively up to 100 elements in the DOM.
is_not_a_child_of.example: Click Element isn't a child of .footer
notes: Available only for the Click Element variable.

is_first_visit.description: Met when the visit qualifies as the visitor's first visit (per Tag Manager / cookie semantics for the configured variable).
notes: Typically used with variables related to first-time vs returning visitors; exact behaviour depends on the variable attached to the condition.
When used with 'View within session' variable it requires numeric string operand value, representing number of minutes.

is_not_first_visit.description: Met when the visit does not qualify as the visitor's first visit.
notes: Typically used with variables related to first-time vs returning visitors; exact behaviour depends on the variable attached to the condition.
When used with 'View within session' variable it requires numeric string operand value, representing number of minutes.

each_time.description: Fire each time the condition is satisfied (e.g. each time a scroll or timer threshold is reached).
notes: Used with built-in variables such as Time on Website (4a3cbab8-e239-44ca-b1c9-6c1bc5cc3fbd) or Page Scroll (a9a87b7d-d565-433d-8090-df9d80bf91f5); set `value` to seconds (timer) or threshold (scroll) per variable documentation.

once_per_page_view.description: Fire at most once per page view when the condition is met.
notes: Used with Time on Website or Page Scroll conditions; see trigger templates for required variable_id, value, and options.

once_per_session.description: Fire at most once per session when the condition is met.
notes: Used with Time on Website or Page Scroll conditions; see trigger templates for required variable_id, value, and options.

visitor_belongs_to.description: Met when the visitor belongs to the specified audience.
notes: Requires Data Activation (audiences). The condition `value` identifies the audience per your Tag Manager configuration.

visitor_not_belongs_to.description: Met when the visitor does not belong to the specified audience.
notes: Requires Data Activation (audiences). The condition `value` identifies the audience per your Tag Manager configuration.

conditions_reference.description: Deduplicated union of optional trigger condition variables documented across trigger templates (`event_conditions_reference.conditions`), keyed by `builtin_variable_name`. Descriptions prefer page_view, then event, then form_submission, then other templates.
mcp_lookup_notes: Each entry's builtin_variable_name is the human-readable built-in variable label; builtin_variable_id is the API variable_id to use in conditions[].variable_id.

When building conditions[] for triggers_create/triggers_update: set variable_id from conditions_reference.conditions.<key>.builtin_variable_id, unless the condition uses a custom app variable (then use variables_list with builtin=false).
Trigger templates reference these keys via available_event_conditions.conditions and required_conditions.*.condition_reference.

campaign.description: Fires when a visitor visits a page to which they were directed by the selected campaign (based on utm_campaign parameter).

cdp_audience.description: Fires a tag whenever it detects that the user is a member of any selected audience. Membership is checked at the beginning of a session and periodically during the session.

click_classes.description: Fires when the visitor clicks an element with the selected CSS class

click_element.description: Fires when the visitor clicks an element matching the selected CSS or XPath selector

click_id.description: Fires when the visitor clicks an element with the selected ID

click_url.description: Fires when the visitor clicks a link with the selected URL

consents.description: Fires when the visitor consents meets given conditions

custom_variable_based.description: Any custom variable can be used to define trigger conditions

event.description: Fires a tag when a specific event occurs in the data layer

external_referrer.description: Fires when a visitor visits a page to which they were directed by the selected external referrer (different domain).

form_classes.description: Fires when a visitor submits a form with the selected CSS class

form_id.description: Fires when a visitor submits a form with the selected ID

form_name.description: Fires when a visitor submits a form with the selected name

form_url.description: Fires when a visitor submits a form that sends a request to the selected page URL

found_elements.description: Fires the tag when the selected element is present on a page. The condition's value is the CSS selector (e.g. .promo_banner or a class name)

history_fragment.description: Fires when the URL hash matches the selected condition

history_source.description: Fires when a specific history event occurs (pushState, replaceState, popState or hashchange)

history_state.description: Fires when the history state matches the selected condition
history_state.example: History state is set or History state equals my-state

leave_content.description: Fires the tag when a visitor moves the cursor in the selected direction. The condition's value must be one of: 'top' (upper page boundary / exit intent), 'any' (upper, bottom or side page boundary).

value_descriptions.top: fires when the cursor leaves via the top of the viewport
value_descriptions.any: fires when the cursor leaves via any edge

old_history_fragment.description: Fires when the previous URL hash matches the selected condition

old_history_state.description: Fires when the previous history state matches the selected condition

page_url.description: Fires when a visitor visits a page with the selected page URL.

page_hostname.description: Fires when a visitor visits a page hosted on the selected domain.

page_path.description: Fires when a visitor visits a page with the selected page path.

page_scroll.description: Fires the tag when a visitor scrolls to the selected point on the page. For example, a visitor scrolls 50% of the page or scrolls down to 1440 px.

unit.description: Unit for the scroll threshold. 'percentage' = percent of page scrolled (value 0–100). 'pixels' = scroll depth in pixels.

referrer.description: Fires when a visitor visits a page to which they were directed by the selected referrer (internal, same domain).

returning_visitor.description: Fires when a visitor is a returning visitor and visits a page. Recognized by Tag Manager using the stg_returning_visitor cookie.

time_on_website.description: Fires the tag when a visitor stays on your site for the selected time (seconds).

traffic_source.description: Fires when a visitor visits a page to which they were directed by the selected traffic source. Possible values: campaign, organic search, social, referral, direct.

value.note: Use values from enum. If copied from UI (not snake-cased, capitalized), they will not work properly.

view_within_session.description: Fires when it is/isn't first visit within session

step_1.purpose: Confirm trigger_type, required_conditions, available_event_conditions, and which builtin_variable_name values apply (see conditions_reference in the merged template).

step_2.action: Resolve built-in variable UUIDs for conditions
step_2.purpose: Copy each built-in conditions[].variable_id from conditions_reference.conditions.<key>.builtin_variable_id before triggers_create. Built-in UUIDs are fixed — do not use variables_list for them.

step_3.purpose: When the trigger allows custom_variable_based or the condition targets a user-created variable, copy the resource id from the list into conditions[].variable_id.

step_4.purpose: Create the trigger with conditions that reference verified variable_id values.

step_5.purpose: Associate the trigger with a tag.

step_6.purpose: Verify trigger conditions fire as expected before going live.
